fix(streams): the last seven io::streams divergences, and the declarations behind them

`io::streams` goes from 7 failures to 0 — 615 tests, and 1015 across the whole `io` module.

STREAM_WRAPPER_REGISTER ACCEPTED EVERYTHING. Both of php's refusal warnings were DECLARED in
`stream_wrapper_register.rs`, emitted into the data section as `_swr_bad_proto_msg` and
`_swr_dup_proto_msg`, and NOTHING BRANCHED TO EITHER. The helper's own comment said "PHP never
refuses a registration", which the measurement disproves three times over. Three sides of the
contract were alive — the strings, their emission, the documentation — and the one that would use
them was never written.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6:

  - a protocol may hold only `[A-Za-z0-9+.-]`: `a_b`, `a b`, `a/b`, `a:b`, `a#b`, a tab, `a$b`,
    `a%b` and any non-ASCII byte are refused; `AB`, `aB`, `a1`, `a+b`, `a-b`, `a.b` pass.
  - an already-registered protocol is refused — a user one, and equally a BUILT-IN: `file`, `php`,
    `data`, `http`, `zip`, `compress.zlib`, `glob`, `ftp` all answer false. Unless it was
    UNREGISTERED, which frees the name, so that half reads the same disabled-wrapper bitmask
    `stream_wrapper_unregister` maintains rather than keeping a second copy of the state.
  - an EMPTY protocol registers successfully, which is why the scan is a per-byte filter rather
    than a "looks like a scheme" test.
  - registration is case-SENSITIVE: `Cd`, `cd` and `CD` are three registrations.

`__rt_diag_warning` takes its message in x1/x2 on AArch64 and rdi/rsi on x86_64. The two arms are
not mirrors of each other and writing them as though they were would have passed a length where a
pointer belongs.

THE CATALOGUE COULD NOT SAY `?int`. php's stub is `stream_select($r, $w, $e, ?int $seconds, ?int
$microseconds = null)`, and `$seconds` was declared plain `Int` because nullability had nowhere to
live — the only thing resembling it is `default: Some(DefaultSpec::Null)`, which says what an
OMITTED argument becomes, and `$seconds` is REQUIRED. So a written `null` was coerced to `0`, and
for this function those are opposite instructions: null blocks forever, `0` returns immediately.
The lowering already refused php's illegal pair by comparing `$seconds` against NULL_SENTINEL; the
guard could never fire because the sentinel never arrived.

`TypeSpec::Nullable` is added rather than declaring `Mixed`, for the reason `TypeSpec::Ptr`'s own
doc gives about this exact trade: a declaration that cannot say what a parameter accepts does not
become silent, it becomes WRONG. `Mixed` would accept `stream_select($r, $w, $e, "abc")`, which php
refuses, and this builtin has no check hook to catch it afterwards. Only `$seconds` moves;
`$microseconds` is OPTIONAL, so the trailing-null truncation already routes an explicit null to the
omitted-argument branch the lowering has.

DROPPING A TRAILING NULL ERASES THE ARGUMENT COUNT, and one builtin reads it.
`stream_context_set_option($c, $array)` is deprecated and `stream_context_set_option($c, $array,
null)` is not — same effect, different arity, and php's notice counts ZEND_NUM_ARGS rather than
consulting the is_null flag. The truncation turned the second call into the first and collected a
deprecation php does not emit. `ARITY_SENSITIVE_BUILTINS` names it, with the measurement: nothing in
the contract can express this, because whether a C implementation reads the flag or the count is a
property of its BODY.
